subject: MAP: Integration build plan (SDK, streaming, tool-calling, structured outputs)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: MAP: Integration build plan (SDK, streaming, tool-calling, structured outputs)

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Per our discussion, I attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the integration milestone: SDK integration, streaming responses, tool-calling, and structured output support. The MAP includes milestones, suggested owners, target dates, and dependencies.

High-level next steps I propose:
- Our teams align on milestones & owners (this thread)
- Redwood provides SDK checklist + streaming best practices (attached)
- Acme confirms internal priority and target close date
- We schedule a 30m engineering sync with Dev to walk the SDK patterns and tool-calling hooks (suggested: week of 11/16)

Attachments: MAP_Draft_v1.pdf, Integration_SOW.xlsx, SDK_checklist.md

Can you confirm owners on your side (engineering & procurement) and a target close date for contract signature? Once we have those, Jordan and I will lock the canary rollout plan and finalize the commercial terms.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

--

Date: 2026-11-11T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Integration build plan (SDK, streaming, tool-calling, structured outputs)

Marissa —

Thanks for sending this over. Quick notes after a first pass:
- The milestones look good.
- We need clarity on the SDK compatibility (Node/Python) and any additional infra reqs for streaming (websockets vs HTTP/2).
- Tool-calling: our platform team will want to understand how Redwood signals structured outputs vs free text; is there a schema enforcement option?
- Procurement needs the SOW line items separated (can you send a redline-friendly XLSX, thanks).

Owners on our side:
- Engineering: Tom Reynolds (copied)
- Platform/Integration lead: Sarah Park
- Procurement: procurement@acmeanalytics.com

Target timeline: we'd like to close commercial terms by 2026-12-10 if all dependencies are aligned. Is that achievable on Redwood's side?

Happy to do the engineering sync next week — Tom and I are available 11/16 or 11/17.

Thanks,
Sarah
Director, Product Integrations | Acme Analytics

> On Nov 10, 2026, at 3:22 PM, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> > [initial email with MAP attachments]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmeanalytics.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Integration build plan (SDK, streaming, tool-calling, structured outputs) — owners & dependencies

Sarah/Tom —

Thanks — I updated the MAP to include more granular owner assignments and a dependency column. Key clarifications:
- SDKs: Redwood supports Node and Python officially; Dev will own the integration guide and test harness.
- Streaming: we support both HTTP/2 server-sent chunks (recommended) and a websocket fallback; Elliot will document recommended patterns and latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Tool-calling/structured outputs: Redwood can emit structured JSON with a shape contract; we recommend a small schema contract agreed in the MAP and we can enforce validation at the SDK layer (Dev owner).

Proposed milestone summary (from updated MAP):
1) SDK integration checklist published (owner: Dev Patel) — target: 2026-11-20
2) Streaming integration guide + sample (owner: Elliot Price) — target: 2026-11-22
3) Tool-calling schema draft (owner: Sarah Park & Dev Patel) — target: 2026-11-24
4) Internal test harness + end-to-end demo (owner: Jordan Blake & Tom Reynolds) — target: 2026-11-30
5) Canaries + rollback plan (owner: Jordan Blake) — target: 2026-12-06

Dependencies called out:
- Acme to provide schema requirements and a sample dataset for validation (dependency for milestone 3).
- Procurement to return SOW redlines by 2026-11-19 (dependency for commercial close).

Jordan and I will coordinate the 30m engineering sync — how does 11/16 at 10:30am PT look for Tom and Dev? If that works we'll send a calendar invite and agenda (SDK patterns + tool-calling walkthrough).

I attached the updated MAP (MAP_Draft_v1.pdf) and a redline-friendly Integration_SOW.xlsx. Let me know if you prefer the MAP as a Google Sheet instead.

Best,
Marissa

--
Attachment: MAP_Draft_v1.pdf, Integration_SOW.xlsx
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sarah Park <sarah.park@acmeanalytics.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T08:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Integration build plan — SDK notes and test harness plan

Hey all —

Thanks for the ownership. A few technical notes from my side to make the engineering sync efficient:
- SDK: we'll publish Node (npm) and Python (pip) packages. Initial runtime targets: Node 16+/Python 3.9+.
- Streaming: we'll provide an HTTP/2 chunked example and a WS example. For low-latency streaming (UI use cases) recommend HTTP/2 client streaming with prefix caching enabled.
- Tool-calling: propose a simple envelope: {\"tool\": \"<name>\", \"payload\": {...}} and an optional \"schemaVersion\" header. I can add an example to the SDK checklist (SDK_checklist.md).
- Tests: please provide a small sample payload (100–200 rows) for schema validation; I'll build a CI workflow that runs contract tests on PRs.

I'm happy to lead the sync on 11/16 at 10:30am PT — I'll send an invite with a 20m agenda: 1) SDK install + quick run 2) streaming demo 3) tool-calling examples 4) next steps for schema/validation.

--
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Integrations | Redwood Inference
